title: Additive coordinates on a group scheme over a ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $U$ an $S$-group scheme, meaning a group object [def-sc-group-scheme] in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme]. For an $A$-algebra $R$, let $L_{A,R}=\operatorname{Spec}R[x]$, using the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring], with its structural map to $S$. For an $R$-algebra $B$ with compatible $A$-structure and $b\in B$, write $p_b:\operatorname{Spec}B\to L_{A,R}$ for the $A$-morphism induced by coefficient extension and $x\mapsto b$. An additive coordinate of $U_R$ is an $S$-morphism $q:L_{A,R}\to U$ such that the square with the structural maps $L_{A,R}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $U\to S$ is Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product], and for every such $B$ and every $b,c\in B$ one has $q(p_{b+c})=q(p_b)q(p_c)$ in $U(B)$. Thus the induced isomorphism $\mathbf A^1_R\simeq U_R$ respects the additive group law. For the multiplicative group $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ [def-sfb-split-torus-over-ring] and a $B$-point $t$, define its coordinate value as the image of the Laurent coordinate $T^1$ under the ring map corresponding to $t$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 4.2.2, printed pp.117–119, affine-line parameter and final additive group-law calculation; formulation as a Cartesian square uses the universal property of base change.
